answer: Let each costly credential, say one earned after a paid hardware audit, register an agent through a zero-knowledge proof that also reveals a nullifier: a hash of the secret credential and the market's name. The mesa market sees no link between agents, yet a second sign-up from the same credential produces the same nullifier, an echo the ledger rejects. A farm's clone count is thus capped by audits bought, not keys minted, and identities can't be pooled to push weight toward the zenith.
